artStyle: Chunky hand-painted low-poly 3D game asset in the style of a 1990s arcade game, with bold simple shapes, flat hand-painted colours and soft painted shading.
notes: Sizes are in metres: height for people, longest edge for everything else.
Everything that only glows, spins, bobs or flashes stays in code: bolts, cannon shells, sweep beam, warning circles, stomp ring, blasts, the Foreman's glowing core and the arena floor.
Every entry has a second look (style 'Mecha Pop') for the Look button; it is exported as <id>_mecha_pop.glb.

entries.name: Tamsin Holt
animations: roll: a small character dives forward into a quick shoulder roll and springs back up into a low crouch

animation_use.run: run (legs; the upper body can play shoot on top)
animation_use.shoot: upper body only, sped up to 6 shots a second

entries.prompt: Chunky hand-painted low-poly 3D game asset in the style of a 1990s arcade game, with bold simple shapes, flat hand-painted colours and soft painted shading. A young woman scrapyard scavenger standing in a T-pose, facing the camera, arms straight out to the sides with open hands, legs straight and slightly apart. Adult proportions, 1.7 metres tall: the head is about one sixth of her height, the arms are long enough to reach mid-thigh when lowered, the body is no wider than the shoulders, with clear space between the arms and the body and between the two legs. She wears a snug patched teal work jumpsuit with the sleeves rolled tight to the elbow, a fitted rust-orange padded vest, a narrow belt with small flat pouches, knee pads, chunky brown work boots and fingerless gloves. Short cropped dark-brown hair close to the head, round welding goggles pushed up flat on the forehead, a smudge of oil on one cheek. Nothing loose or hanging: no scarf, no cape, no long hair, no straps or tails, and nothing held in the hands, single isolated object, centered, on a plain white background

entries.prompt: Chunky hand-painted low-poly 3D game asset in the style of a 1990s arcade game, with bold simple shapes, flat hand-painted colours and soft painted shading. A small four-legged robot hound built from mismatched scrap, seen in a three-quarter front view, standing square with all four legs straight down and spread apart. 1.4 metres long from nose to tail, 0.8 metres tall and 0.6 metres wide; the body is a short horizontal oil drum, about twice as long as it is tall. busiestMoment.when: Wave 2: Tamsin, 4 hounds, the sleeping Foreman, 6 crate stacks, all 20 wall segments and up to 3 repair kits (the boss fight has no hounds, so it is lighter)

textureMemory.assumption: each GLB has a base-colour, a normal and a metal/roughness map; one map with mipmaps takes about 22 MB at 2K, 5.6 MB at 1K and 1.4 MB at 512. All hounds share one texture set, so do all walls, crates and so on.
textureMemory.as exported, 2K, one look: 8 models x 3 maps x 22 MB = about 540 MB
textureMemory.plan: Keep only the active look in memory (the other loads when you press Look). Shrink textures when loading: desktop keeps 2K for Tamsin and the Foreman and uses 1K for the rest; phones use 1K for Tamsin and the Foreman and 512 for the rest.

busiestMoment.phoneVerdict: Yes. About 115,000 triangles is well within what a phone from the last five years draws at 60 frames a second, and with the texture plan the textures need about 60 MB. Without the plan (full 2K, both looks) textures alone would need about 1 GB, which most phones cannot handle. Real numbers will be measured from the actual files in stage 5, especially how many textures the split models bring.
